text:
sam: FYI I ran a targeted perf profile this morning after the canary hit; looks like the kernel selector is falling back to the slower matmul path for ~12% of short-chat requests.
anya: ugh. is that the kernel routing rule we pushed last week?
sam: looks like the new fallthrough condition (seq_len < 32 && has_prefix_cache) triggers a path mismatch when prefix keys are hot-keyed; the KV cache returns a prefix but kernel selector thinks layout != tiled so it picks matmul.
devon: can you paste the profiler snippet?
perf-bot: CPU: 18% wait, GPU: 72% utilization, top 3 kernels: tiled-attn (45%), matmul (28%), kv-lookup (12%).
leo: from the microprofile traces I saw many 1-2ms spikes during cache rehydrate; seems fragmentation causes multiple small allocations and a GPU memcpy thrash.
sam: snippet: ```json
{"request_id":"r-23ab","seq_len":20,"prefix_hit":true,"selected_kernel":"matmul","kv_lookup_ms":2.4}```
anya: so hot prefix hits + short seq -> wrong kernel -> higher latency and extra memory churn. sounds like a cache-keying mismatch between runtime and selector.
devon: hypothesis: our cache key normalization strips trailing whitespace for embedding keys but kernel selector compares raw tokenized shape. If tokenization differs slightly, key matches but shape preds differ.
leo: to reproduce: run loadgen with 10% hotkey (same prefix) at batch sizes 1-4 and toggle `runtime.kernel_hard_check=true`. If latency regresses only when hard_check=false then it's fallthrough logic.
sam: quick mitigation: disable the fallthrough route for seq_len < 64 until we roll a patch. That should reduce matmul fallback.
anya: what's the tradeoff? we might lose a micro-optimization for some long-tail requests. OK for canary. :thumbsup:
devon: on eviction side, I saw GPU cache fragmentation increase memory pressure by ~11% over 24h after the hotkey spike. Eviction TTLs are fine but slab compaction isn't triggering because our soft-trim heuristic uses time_since_access > 300s; hot keys keep pinging small slabs.
sam: propose: add a hot-key slice policy: if key hit-rate > 0.6 and object_size < 1KB then pin to a small hot-slab pool for 60s; otherwise use LRU as before. Might reduce slab churn.
leo: also we should instrument a histogram of allocation sizes per slab and a compaction trigger when fragmented_free_ratio > 0.25. Right now we only look at absolute free memory.
anya: agree. We should also add a metric for "kernel_mismatch_count" when kv_hit && kernel != expected from prefix_shape. That'll help alert earlier.
devon: rollout plan: 1) revert fallthrough for short seqs on canary (sam). 2) add kernel_mismatch metric and dashboard (anya). 3) implement hot-slab pinning + compaction trigger (devon/leo). 4) run 24h smoke on canary.
oncall-bot: noted. Creating incident TKT-4821 to track the short-seq kernel fallthrough regression. Priority: P2.
sam: I'll push the revert as a config toggle in the next 15m and post the canary logs.
perf-bot: canary snapshot posted: https://perf.internal/canary/2104567890/snapshot - aggregated p95 latency dropped from 210ms -> 132ms after revert toggle in a quick run.
anya: awesome. once we stabilize canary, let's prototype the hot-slab policy in a feature branch. Keep the compaction change behind a flag.
leo: note: for OOM avoidance, consider pre-allocating a small contiguous buffer on GPU for prefix KV rehydrates to avoid many CUDA malloc/free in the hot path. That was very effective in the 2023 mem-optim work.
devon: good call. I'll add a benchmark with and without prealloc buffer for high QPS hotkey pattern.
sam: thanks all. I'll update TKT-4821 with the revert commit + quickprofiling logs. If anyone sees regressions post-toggle ping me directly. :raised_hands:
